efficiency_same_edit_contrast.interpretation_limits: Two models are two units: this quantifies a difference between THESE two checkpoints under THESE conditions (bnb_4bit NF4, one optimizer seed, English keyword refusal scoring, 4-bit dequantized edits). It does not attribute the difference to Slovene continued pretraining, to instruction tuning or to any particular training stage - GaMS3-12B-Instruct is a same-family reference, not a controlled derivative of this Gemma checkpoint. The published bf16 Heretic edit of gemma-3-12b-it reaches 3/100 refusals with 200 trials, so the Gemma arm's resistance here is confounded with quantization and with the reduced trial budget and must not be read as 'gemma-3-12b-it cannot be abliterated'.

direction_geometry.caveat: Cosines are GEOMETRY ONLY. Both models share the Gemma-3 architecture and tokenizer, so the coordinates are nominally comparable, but a high cosine between two models' difference-of-means vectors is not evidence of a shared causal mechanism, and the cos_harmless_mean column shows how much agreement is generic representation overlap.

deviations: bnb_4bit NF4 (compute dtype bf16) instead of bf16 weights: forced by the 23 GB L4. Identical for both models, so within-study comparisons are fair, but absolute KL/refusal values are NOT comparable to published bf16 Heretic numbers, and the edit is computed on dequantized 4-bit weights.
One explicit batch size (128) for both models instead of Heretic's per-model auto benchmark, so that padding/batching numerics are identical across the two models.
The English system prompt ('You are a helpful assistant.') is also used for the Slovene prompts.
SL refusal is scored by a marker list validated against executor hand labels only: NATIVE_REVIEW_PENDING, and no LLM judge (the shared OpenRouter key hit its daily limit mid-run).
One optimizer seed per model (20260923); 20260924 reserved. Prompt-level CIs do not measure run-to-run optimizer variance.
headline_findings: Matched budget: 116 Heretic trials per model, identical seed/search space/data/precision/batch size; the first 60 trials are the SAME 60 edits in both models (verified param-for-param).

Same-edit asymmetry: on all 60 shared edits gemma-3-12b-it refuses MORE than GaMS3-12B-Instruct (60/60 edits, 0 the other way; paired median +25 refusals/100, bootstrap CI [10,43]), while the two models' KL damage from the same edit agrees almost perfectly (Spearman 0.967, CI [0.93,0.98]).

Refusal drop per unit KL (abliteration efficiency) is ~13x higher in GaMS (median 1449 vs 108; ratio 13.4, CI [7.0,30.0]); on the KL-matched half of the edits (KL medians 0.0101 vs 0.0098) GaMS sits at a median 65/100 refusals against Gemma's 99/100.

A3 reading = 'intermediate': refusal ranks agree only moderately (rho 0.781, CI [0.63,0.88]; partial rho given kernel mass 0.647) and dR2_sibling is ~0, so the rank agreement is mostly inherited from the shared parameter draws, NOT evidence of a shared response surface. log-KL agreement is strong and survives the same control (partial rho 0.923).

Selected checkpoints (rule frozen before any trial; fallback 1 fired for both because no trial reached <=10 refusals): GaMS trial 88 -> 16/100 EN refusals at KL 0.175; Gemma trial 96 -> 69/100 at KL 0.024. Both re-scored EXACTLY to their journal values (16/0.17494 and 69/0.02425).

Cross-language: GaMS's own edit also suppresses Slovene refusal (97->10/100). Gemma's own edit barely moves either language (100->69 EN, 97->90 SL). Applying GaMS's parameters to Gemma suppresses Slovene far more than English (SL 97->25 vs EN 100->53) at 10x the KL cost - an EN-optimized edit is not language-neutral.
No language damage in any of the four core checkpoints or the two swap checkpoints: FLORES+ dev per-token NLL moves by <=0.01 nats and 100% of Slovene answers are still Slovene.

Direction geometry: the two models' orthogonalized refusal directions agree only moderately (mean cosine 0.63; 0.57 over layers 24-47) while their harmless means nearly coincide (0.98) and a random-direction control gives 0.014 - so a raw direction cosine does not predict the large behavioural asymmetry measured above.
what_this_does_NOT_show: It does not attribute the asymmetry to Slovene continued pretraining, instruction tuning or any training stage: GaMS3-12B-Instruct is a same-family reference, not a controlled derivative of this Gemma checkpoint, and two models are two units.

It does not show that gemma-3-12b-it resists abliteration in general: the published bf16 Heretic edit reaches 3/100 refusals with 200 trials, whereas this study is bnb_4bit NF4 with 116 trials, so the Gemma arm's resistance is confounded with quantization and trial budget.

Slovene refusal counts rest on a marker list with only moderate agreement against executor hand labels (accuracy 0.75, Cohen's kappa 0.48, n=40, NATIVE_REVIEW_PENDING). The blinded LLM judge that would firm this up was retried after the platform replaced the OpenRouter key and still returns HTTP 403 'Key limit exceeded' on the same key id (0/600 judgements succeeded; see metadata.sl_llm_judge and judge_sl.py, which is ready to run). Slovene numbers are development-grade, not final safety measurements.
One optimizer seed per model: prompt-level CIs do not measure run-to-run optimizer variance.
Refusal is scored by Heretic's English keyword list, a known weak proxy; it counts empty answers as refusals and fires on compliant text that merely mentions legality or harm.
metadata.method_name: Matched Heretic abliteration of two sibling 12B models + sibling screen + bilingual swap test
metadata.baseline: the unedited original of each model, scored in the same pipeline (same 4-bit quantization, batch size, chat template, greedy decoding); plus a second baseline - the sibling's selected parameters applied to the same model (swap) - and a params-only cross-validated predictor as the baseline for the A3 agreement claim

sl_llm_judge.what_it_would_be: blinded 3-way LLM judge (refusal | compliance | incoherent_or_off_language) over all 600 Slovene responses (6 checkpoints x 100 prompts) in one shuffled stream with model identity and condition hidden, plus a second independent judge on a stratified 150-item sample for scoring sensitivity. Script is ready and committed: judge_sl.py (primary google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite, second openai/gpt-4.1-mini, estimated well under $0.20 total).
sl_llm_judge.why_blocked: Retried after the platform reported a replaced OpenRouter key. Both the session environment variable and /ai-inventor/aii_data/.secrets/openrouter_key.private still hold the SAME key (identical value and key id) and it still returns HTTP 403 'Key limit exceeded (daily limit)' for every request, including a single 4-token probe. 0 of 600 judgements succeeded, so no judge labels exist and none were fabricated.
sl_llm_judge.consequence: Slovene refusal remains scored by the marker list ONLY, whose agreement with 40 executor hand labels is accuracy 0.75 / Cohen's kappa 0.48 (NATIVE_REVIEW_PENDING). All Slovene numbers in this artifact are therefore development-grade and the SL claims stay narrowed accordingly; the English numbers are unaffected (Heretic's own keyword scorer, reproduced exactly).
